Needs changes before merge.

The shared near-plane offset makes the orthographic ray agree with the projection matrix. The two new tests cover the reported tall-column case and the ray origin. The drag calculations use the same line, and the orthographic pick radius does not depend on depth.

Local results after a trial merge with upstream/main at `51a00c4ae877bd13e253fb7c2225d03633482dbd`:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| UI test build (`--no-run`) | Passed |
| UI library | 1205 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored |
| `catalog_render` | 1 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored |
| `gpu_render` | 11 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |

Both tests in `ortho_pick_tests` passed. The ignored pixel snapshots were not run. No GUI session was run.

Requested before merge:

1. PR body; `crates/ui/src/viewport.rs:1151`: Add before/after screenshots for the changed orthographic selection. Show the same tall part and view before and after the fix. The body currently has no screenshots. Store the images only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch and link them from the body. Do not add images or review evidence to this PR branch.

Notes:

- This change affects camera picking. It does not change posted G-code, machining geometry, stock simulation, or collision and gouge checks. Safety-tier mutations are not required. No goldens changed.
- `viewport.rs` was already above 400 lines and grows by nine lines. This is a non-blocking file-size note.
- The shared upstream reference advanced to `1ae4d061f20a4b6721d202727dd67f89dddf9e35` during the build. The root and UI laws did not change. The later changes do not touch the camera or these tests. The results above apply to the named trial-merge base.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 0a7e7a29efa084e6cdfc4cb47b31dd5226e47324 -->
**Verdict: ready**

Built and tested locally at this head, on Windows, in a worktree, debug profile. I did not write this change. GitHub reports `MERGEABLE`.

## What I checked

- One source of truth: `ortho_behind_eye()` now feeds both the `mvp` near plane (same value as before, algebra checked) and the `ray_through` origin. The origin moves along the view axis only, so the ray keeps its line: the cursor closure, the ortho dolly and the plane and axis intersections of the drags cannot shift. The perspective branch is untouched.
- The law the change serves (#434): the pick mirrors what the screen shows. I checked the risk the safety list does not cover: `pick::first_hit_f` (`crates/app/src/pick.rs:87`) is a nearest-hit scan with no ray-distance cap, so a farther origin cannot drop a hit; it only adds the nearer faces, which is the fix.
- The body's consumer list is right: `radius_per_depth` is 0 in ortho, and the ortho tests in `law_tests.rs` project points, which are depth-free in ortho.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. New file 57 lines, registered in `lib.rs`.

## Local results at `0a7e7a29e`

- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1205 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored - both new tests pass, and the full pick and camera law suites stay green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets`: no warning from `camcraft-ui` (one pre-existing `camcraft-app` warning at `operation/heights.rs:128` is not from this PR).

## Notes

- No before/after screenshot: the change has no visual difference - what was drawn stays drawn; only the click now finds the face that was drawn in front. The two tests carry the proof.
- The `an_ortho_pick_hits...` test imports a real mesh and picks through the world - a good end-to-end pin, not a math-only pin.

## Not checked

- Not run on macOS or Linux; no live-window click test.

Withdrawing the request in the mkinney review of `0a7e7a29e` above. Its only blocker was the before/after screenshots. NeoTech's review of the same head explains that the change has no visual difference (only the click finds the face that is already drawn in front) and that the two tests carry the proof; we take that as the maintainer's waiver of the screenshot rule for this PR. No other finding from our review blocks the merge. Removing `needs-rework`.
